subject: Roadmap gap credit request — streaming pipelining delay
messages:
From: Dana Smythe <dana.smythe@finlytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Streaming pipelining delay — request for credit while we wait

Hannah,

Thanks for the call this morning. As we discussed, our integration depends on the streaming-pipelining v2 feature (low-latency token streaming + prefix-resumption) that your team committed to in Q3. Per the roadmap update, the feature is slipping into late Q1 next year.

This delay materially impacts our production SLA and user rollout plan. We have already postponed three customer launches and incurred extra engineering effort on our side to maintain a custom poll/flush workaround.

Request: Finlytics is asking for a one-time credit to offset the additional engineering and go-to-market costs, equivalent to 25% of our October–December projected usage (we've attached a usage snapshot). We believe this is a reasonable mitigation while Redwood ships pipelining v2.

If needed, we can accept a temporary account-level discount applied until the feature ships, or a one-time invoice credit — whatever is easiest for your billing/finance team.

Can you route this to the appropriate approvals? We need confirmation before our next sprint planning (Nov 30) to decide whether to re-scope the launch or push further.

Appreciate your help,

—Dana
Director of Integrations
Finlytics

Attachments:
- finlytics_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Streaming pipelining delay — request for credit while we wait

Team — forwarding Finlytics' ask. TL;DR: customer requests either a temporary account discount or one-time credit until streaming-pipelining v2 is delivered (timeline has slipped).

Quick context: Finlytics is a strategic mid-market account; usage profile high spike in Q4, public-facing product with a lot of PR sensitivity. We committed to more concrete ETA in Q3 roadmap comms; product has moved that to late Q1.

Actions I need from you:
- Laura: confirm technical ETA and any scope-bands (is there a partial rollout we can promise?)
- Dev: feasibility of an interim smaller change (e.g., improved prefix cache + 50ms reduction) that we could ship sooner
- Markus: what finance needs to approve a one-time credit vs. temporary discount; rough revenue impact estimate
- Connor: suggested commercial wording and next steps with Finlytics (I want to stay in a positive posture)

I'll draft an approval packet for execs if we decide to go that route. If anyone needs more context from the Finlytics thread, let me know.

Thanks — Hannah
Head of Sales Ops (interim)
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Streaming pipelining delay — request for credit while we wait

Hannah / team,

Thanks — short answer on ETA: current schedule targets a beta of streaming-pipelining v2 in mid-February (2027-02-15) with GA end of March. There's risk on infra perf validation that could push GA into April.

We do have a smaller rollout path: a lightweight prefix-resumption shim + kv-cache flush improvements that Dev estimates could land in early January if we prioritize it. That would reduce customer pain but not fully restore their original low-latency behavior.

Given that, my recommendation: offer a temporary, explicit mitigation (e.g., 10–15% account-level discount) for the period until we have the January shim; reassess for an additional, smaller one-time credit if GA slips beyond March.

I'm happy to provide a short technical note for the approval packet describing the partial shim and known gaps.

-Laura
Product Lead, Serving
Redwood Inference

Folks,

I've looked at the shim option. Work estimate: ~3 engineer-weeks for a focused effort (1 week spec + 2 weeks implementation + QA). We can scope it to prioritized customers (Finlytics being top) and ship a toggled rollout.

Risks: the shim complicates the runtime code paths and we need to ensure it doesn't regress existing high-throughput jobs. Also there's a small chance it won't fully meet Finlytics' SLA needs; we should set clear expectations.

If leadership wants to move fast, product should commit the priority and we can deliver a beta by 2027-01-10.

-Dev

Hannah / team,

Thanks for the context. A few points from finance:
- One-time credit: usually needs Director+ approval depending on size; create an approval packet showing net revenue impact and rationale.
- Temporary discount (account-level): operationally simpler — we can implement a timed pricing override in Billing for up to 90 days without exec sign-off for discounts < 20% of ARR footprint. Above 20% triggers finance + legal review.
- We need to capture the mitigation approach in a short MOP (mechanism of performance) so our billing team can reconcile when the feature ships (i.e., when to stop the discount or apply clawback, if agreed).

Attached: proposed_credit_sheet.xlsx (stub in thread) — includes quick impact math based on the usage snapshot.

If you want me to take this to approval, I can prepare the packet; tell me the suggested discount cadence and any commercial language.

-Markus
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Hannah — draft commercial stance to take to Finlytics:
1) Offer a time-bound 12% account-level discount effective immediately, to be applied through 2027-02-28.
2) Commit to the engineering shim beta by 2027-01-10; if beta meets agreed metrics, we stop the discount on 2027-02-28.
3) If GA slips beyond March 31, offer a one-time invoice credit equal to an additional 8% of Q1 usage (to be calculated post-quarter).

This keeps the ask modest, gives Finlytics immediate mitigation, and preserves our ability to limit long-term revenue impact. Markus: does this fit the <20% rule you mentioned?

If we agree, I can present to VP Sales (Aditya Rao) for signoff and include a short exec summary. I'll attach the commercial bullets in an email to Finlytics and propose a 30-minute alignment call.

-Connor
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

I authorize Markus to prepare the official packet and legal to draft a short amendment to the existing T&Cs describing the temporary pricing override and conditions. Connor — please schedule the customer alignment call for tomorrow.
